vocabulary.meaning: A round fruit that is red, green or yellow.
vocabulary.explanation: An apple is crunchy and sweet. It grows on a tree!
vocabulary.usage: You can say: 'Can I have an apple, please?'

vocabulary.meaning: A round toy that you throw, kick or bounce.
vocabulary.explanation: A ball is round. You can play catch with it!
vocabulary.usage: At the park: 'Throw the ball to me!'

vocabulary.meaning: A small furry animal that says 'meow'.
vocabulary.explanation: A cat has soft fur, whiskers and a long tail.

vocabulary.meaning: A friendly animal that barks.
vocabulary.explanation: A dog wags its tail when it is happy!

vocabulary.meaning: Feeling good and full of joy.
vocabulary.explanation: When you smile and laugh, you are happy!
vocabulary.usage: Tell a friend: 'I am happy to see you!'

vocabulary.meaning: Feeling unhappy.
vocabulary.explanation: When you feel like crying, you feel sad.
vocabulary.usage: You can say: 'I feel sad. Can I have a hug?'

vocabulary.meaning: Large in size.
vocabulary.explanation: An elephant is big. A mouse is not!

vocabulary.meaning: Little in size.
vocabulary.explanation: An ant is small. You can hold it on one finger!

vocabulary.meaning: The big bright star that gives us light in the day.
vocabulary.explanation: The sun shines in the sky and keeps us warm.
vocabulary.usage: In the morning say: 'The sun is up!'

vocabulary.meaning: The bright round thing we see in the night sky.
vocabulary.explanation: At night, look up! The moon is glowing.

vocabulary.meaning: A tiny twinkling light in the night sky.
vocabulary.explanation: Stars twinkle, twinkle at night!
vocabulary.usage: Make a wish on a star!

vocabulary.meaning: A tall plant with a trunk, branches and leaves.
vocabulary.explanation: Birds make nests in trees. Trees give us shade!

vocabulary.meaning: An animal that lives and swims in water.
vocabulary.explanation: A fish swims with its fins and tail.
vocabulary.usage: At an aquarium: 'Look at the orange fish!'

vocabulary.meaning: An animal with feathers and wings that can fly.
vocabulary.explanation: Birds sing 'tweet tweet' in the morning!
vocabulary.example: A bird is on the tree.

vocabulary.meaning: To push yourself up into the air with your legs.
vocabulary.explanation: Bend your knees and jump up high like a frog!
vocabulary.usage: In a game: 'Jump over the line!'

vocabulary.meaning: To move very fast on your feet.
vocabulary.explanation: When you run, your legs go fast fast fast!

vocabulary.meaning: Very warm.
vocabulary.explanation: Fire is hot. Do not touch it!

vocabulary.meaning: Not warm; chilly.
vocabulary.explanation: Ice cream is cold. Brrr!
vocabulary.usage: Say: 'I feel cold. I need a sweater.'

vocabulary.meaning: To make a happy face with your mouth.
vocabulary.explanation: When you smile, your lips curve up like a rainbow!

vocabulary.meaning: Pages with words and pictures that you read.
vocabulary.explanation: A book has stories inside it!

vocabulary.meaning: A sweet, soft food we eat on birthdays.
vocabulary.explanation: On your birthday, you blow candles on a cake!
vocabulary.usage: Say: 'Happy birthday! Let's cut the cake!'

vocabulary.meaning: Drops of water falling from clouds.
vocabulary.explanation: In the monsoon, rain goes pitter-patter!
vocabulary.usage: Say: 'Take your umbrella, it is raining!'

vocabulary.meaning: Something you wear on your head.
vocabulary.explanation: A hat keeps the sun off your head.
vocabulary.usage: Say: 'Wear your hat, it is sunny!'

vocabulary.meaning: A machine with four wheels that people ride in.
vocabulary.explanation: A car goes vroom vroom on the road!

vocabulary.meaning: A white drink that comes from cows.
vocabulary.explanation: Milk makes your bones strong!
vocabulary.usage: Say: 'May I have a glass of milk?'

vocabulary.meaning: To make music with your voice.
vocabulary.explanation: La la la! When you sing, you make music.

vocabulary.meaning: To hit your hands together to make a sound.
vocabulary.explanation: Clap clap! We clap when someone does well.

vocabulary.meaning: A water bird that says 'quack'.
vocabulary.explanation: A duck swims in the pond and says quack quack!

vocabulary.meaning: The colourful part of a plant.
vocabulary.explanation: Flowers smell nice. Bees love them!

vocabulary.meaning: Someone you like and play with.
vocabulary.explanation: A friend shares toys and makes you laugh!

vocabulary.meaning: Not afraid to do something hard or scary.
vocabulary.explanation: When you try something new even if you feel scared, you are brave!
vocabulary.example: The brave girl climbed the tall slide.
vocabulary.usage: Say: 'I was brave at the doctor today!'

vocabulary.meaning: Kind and soft, not rough.
vocabulary.explanation: Be gentle with a puppy — touch it softly.
vocabulary.usage: Say: 'Please be gentle with my book.'

vocabulary.meaning: Fast; done in a short time.
vocabulary.explanation: A cheetah is quick. Zoom!
vocabulary.usage: Say: 'Be quick, the bus is here!'

vocabulary.meaning: To laugh in a light, silly way.
vocabulary.explanation: Tee-hee! When something is funny, you giggle.
vocabulary.example: The babies giggle at the clown.

vocabulary.meaning: To speak very softly.
vocabulary.explanation: Shh! When you whisper, only someone close can hear.
vocabulary.example: She whispered a secret to me.

vocabulary.meaning: To say something very loudly.
vocabulary.explanation: When you shout, everyone can hear you!
vocabulary.usage: On the field: 'Shout if you need help!'

vocabulary.meaning: Full of light or shining strongly.
vocabulary.explanation: The sun is bright — it makes you squint!
vocabulary.example: The room is bright and sunny.

vocabulary.meaning: Wanting to know or learn about something.
vocabulary.explanation: When you ask 'Why? How?', you are curious!
vocabulary.example: The curious cat looked inside the box.

vocabulary.meaning: Very, very small.
vocabulary.explanation: An ant is tiny. A ladybug is tiny too!

vocabulary.meaning: Tasting very good.
vocabulary.explanation: Yum! When food tastes super good, it is delicious.

vocabulary.meaning: A place where flowers, plants or vegetables grow.
vocabulary.explanation: In a garden you can find flowers, bees and butterflies!
vocabulary.example: We planted seeds in the garden.

vocabulary.meaning: A small pool of water on the ground.
vocabulary.explanation: After the rain, you can splash in a puddle!

vocabulary.meaning: A curve of colours in the sky after rain.
vocabulary.explanation: A rainbow has seven colours, like a sky ribbon!
vocabulary.example: We saw a rainbow after the rain.

vocabulary.meaning: To shine with tiny flashes of light.
vocabulary.explanation: Glitter and diamonds sparkle in the light!

vocabulary.meaning: To move from side to side in a shaky way.
vocabulary.explanation: Jelly wobbles when you shake the plate!

vocabulary.meaning: Warm, soft and comfortable.
vocabulary.explanation: Snuggling in a blanket feels cozy!
vocabulary.example: My bed is warm and cozy.

vocabulary.meaning: Showing good manners.
vocabulary.explanation: Saying 'please' and 'thank you' is polite!
vocabulary.example: Rohan is always polite to his teachers.

vocabulary.meaning: To let others use or have some of what you have.
vocabulary.explanation: When you share your crayons, everyone can colour!
vocabulary.usage: Say: 'Do you want to share my snack?'

vocabulary.meaning: To go around a new place to find out about it.
vocabulary.explanation: Explorers look around new places to discover things!

vocabulary.meaning: To bring things together and keep them.
vocabulary.explanation: Some children collect stamps, shells or stickers!

vocabulary.meaning: Making little or no noise.
vocabulary.explanation: In the library we stay quiet — shh!
vocabulary.usage: Say: 'Please be quiet, the baby is sleeping.'

vocabulary.meaning: Having lots of power; not weak.
vocabulary.explanation: An elephant is strong — it can lift a log!

vocabulary.meaning: Hard to lift because it weighs a lot.
vocabulary.explanation: A big bag of rice is heavy!
vocabulary.usage: Say: 'Can you help me? This box is heavy.'

vocabulary.meaning: Having nothing inside.
vocabulary.explanation: When your glass has no water, it is empty.

vocabulary.meaning: Ready and happy to help.
vocabulary.explanation: When you help Mom set the table, you are helpful!
vocabulary.usage: Say: 'Thank you, you are so helpful!'

vocabulary.meaning: Paying attention so nothing goes wrong.
vocabulary.explanation: Be careful when you cross the road — look both ways!

vocabulary.meaning: A trip from one place to another.
vocabulary.explanation: Going to your grandma's town by train is a journey!

vocabulary.meaning: To fall down suddenly and roll.
vocabulary.explanation: Oops! The toys tumbled off the shelf.
vocabulary.example: Jack and Jill tumbled down the hill.

vocabulary.meaning: A special day or time of celebration.
vocabulary.explanation: Diwali, Eid, Christmas and Pongal are festivals!
vocabulary.example: Holi is a festival of colours.
vocabulary.usage: Say: 'Which festival do you like best?'

vocabulary.meaning: A person who lives next to you or near you.
vocabulary.explanation: The people next door are your neighbours.
vocabulary.example: Our neighbour has a cute puppy.

vocabulary.meaning: Extremely big.
vocabulary.explanation: Bigger than big — like an elephant or a blue whale!

vocabulary.meaning: Extremely beautiful and impressive.
vocabulary.explanation: The Taj Mahal is magnificent — it makes you say 'Wow!'
vocabulary.example: The palace looked magnificent at night.

vocabulary.meaning: An exciting or unusual experience.
vocabulary.explanation: Exploring a jungle or a cave is an adventure!
vocabulary.example: Our camping trip was a real adventure.

vocabulary.meaning: The ability to do something that frightens you.
vocabulary.explanation: Courage is being brave even when your knees shake!
vocabulary.example: It takes courage to speak on stage.

vocabulary.meaning: Very, very old.
vocabulary.explanation: Dinosaurs lived in ancient times — millions of years ago!
vocabulary.example: We visited an ancient temple in Hampi.

vocabulary.meaning: Easily broken or damaged.
vocabulary.explanation: Glass and eggs are fragile — handle with care!
vocabulary.usage: A label might say: 'Fragile — handle with care.'

vocabulary.meaning: Strange and hard to explain.
vocabulary.explanation: A locked box with no key is mysterious!
vocabulary.example: We heard a mysterious sound in the attic.
vocabulary.usage: Say: 'This story has a mysterious ending.'

vocabulary.meaning: Very surprised.
vocabulary.explanation: When something amazes you so much your mouth drops open!
vocabulary.example: I was astonished by the magic trick.
vocabulary.usage: Say: 'I was astonished to see snow!'

vocabulary.meaning: Happy to give and share with others.
vocabulary.explanation: A generous person shares their things kindly.
vocabulary.example: My generous uncle bought books for everyone.
vocabulary.usage: Say: 'That was very generous of you!'

vocabulary.meaning: To disappear suddenly.
vocabulary.explanation: Poof! The magician made the rabbit vanish!
vocabulary.example: The rainbow vanished after a few minutes.

vocabulary.meaning: To shine faintly.
vocabulary.explanation: A tiny light that shines softly is glimmering.
vocabulary.usage: Say: 'I saw a light glimmer far away.'

vocabulary.meaning: Careful to avoid danger.
vocabulary.explanation: A cautious person looks carefully before doing something.
vocabulary.example: Be cautious near the river bank.
vocabulary.usage: Say: 'Be cautious on the wet floor.'

vocabulary.meaning: Very pleased and happy.
vocabulary.explanation: When you get exactly the gift you wanted, you are delighted!
vocabulary.example: She was delighted with her medal.
vocabulary.usage: Say: 'I am delighted to meet you!'

vocabulary.meaning: Not giving up until you succeed.
vocabulary.explanation: Trying again and again to ride a cycle means you are determined!
vocabulary.example: He was determined to win the race.
vocabulary.usage: Say: 'I am determined to finish my project.'

vocabulary.meaning: Extremely interesting.
vocabulary.explanation: Something so interesting you can't stop looking at it!

vocabulary.meaning: Dark, dull or sad.
vocabulary.explanation: A grey, cloudy day can feel gloomy.
vocabulary.example: The sky was gloomy before the storm.
vocabulary.usage: Say: 'Why are you looking so gloomy?'

vocabulary.meaning: The time when crops are gathered from the fields.
vocabulary.explanation: Farmers collect rice and wheat at harvest. Pongal and Baisakhi are harvest festivals!
vocabulary.example: The harvest was good this year.
vocabulary.usage: Say: 'Farmers are busy during the harvest.'

vocabulary.meaning: To make a picture of something in your mind.
vocabulary.explanation: Close your eyes and imagine a flying elephant!
vocabulary.example: Imagine you could fly over the city.
vocabulary.usage: Say: 'Imagine if we lived on the moon!'

vocabulary.meaning: Always supporting and standing by someone.
vocabulary.explanation: A loyal friend is always on your side.
vocabulary.usage: Say: 'Thanks for being a loyal friend.'

vocabulary.meaning: Wonderful; extremely good.
vocabulary.explanation: Something so good it makes you cheer!
vocabulary.example: We had a marvellous time at the fair.

vocabulary.meaning: Worried or a little afraid about something.
vocabulary.explanation: Butterflies in your tummy before a test? That is feeling nervous.
vocabulary.example: I felt nervous before my dance show.

vocabulary.meaning: Strange or unusual.
vocabulary.explanation: A cat that barks would be peculiar!
vocabulary.example: There was a peculiar smell in the kitchen.

vocabulary.meaning: To save someone from danger.
vocabulary.explanation: Firefighters rescue people and even kittens stuck in trees!
vocabulary.example: The team rescued the puppy from the drain.

vocabulary.meaning: To throw or spread things in many directions.
vocabulary.explanation: When you drop marbles, they scatter everywhere!
vocabulary.usage: Say: 'Don't scatter your toys on the floor.'

vocabulary.meaning: Moving very fast.
vocabulary.explanation: A swift bird zips through the sky like an arrow!
vocabulary.example: The swift horse won the race.

vocabulary.meaning: Shy and easily frightened.
vocabulary.explanation: A timid mouse hides when people come near.
vocabulary.example: The timid kitten hid under the bed.

vocabulary.meaning: To walk around slowly without a fixed plan.
vocabulary.explanation: Wandering is walking here and there just to look around!
vocabulary.usage: Say: 'Don't wander away from the group.'

vocabulary.meaning: Wanting to do something very much.
vocabulary.explanation: When you can't wait to open your birthday gifts, you are eager!
vocabulary.example: The students were eager to start the experiment.

vocabulary.meaning: Unusual in a way that gets attention.
vocabulary.explanation: Something so special that people talk about it!

vocabulary.meaning: To keep someone or something safe.
vocabulary.explanation: A helmet protects your head when you cycle!

vocabulary.meaning: Continuing to try even when something is difficult.
vocabulary.explanation: Practising a hard piano piece every day until you get it right — that's perseverance.
vocabulary.example: Her perseverance helped her solve the tough puzzle.
vocabulary.usage: A coach might say: 'Perseverance wins matches.'

vocabulary.meaning: Able to recover quickly from difficulties.
vocabulary.explanation: A resilient person bounces back like a rubber ball after a setback.
vocabulary.example: The resilient team won after losing the first match.
vocabulary.usage: Say: 'Plants in the desert are resilient.'

vocabulary.meaning: Able to speak or write clearly and beautifully.
vocabulary.explanation: An eloquent speaker chooses words so well that people love to listen.
vocabulary.example: Her eloquent speech moved the audience.

vocabulary.meaning: Having more than one possible meaning.
vocabulary.explanation: 'I saw her duck' is ambiguous — a bird, or did she bend down?
vocabulary.example: The question was ambiguous, so I asked the teacher.
vocabulary.usage: Say: 'Your instructions are a bit ambiguous.'

vocabulary.meaning: Kind and wanting to do good for others.
vocabulary.explanation: A benevolent person helps others without expecting anything back.
vocabulary.example: The benevolent king built schools for every village.
vocabulary.usage: Say: 'The benevolent donor funded the library.'

vocabulary.meaning: Very careful about every small detail.
vocabulary.explanation: A meticulous person checks everything twice and keeps things perfectly neat.
vocabulary.example: Riya is meticulous about her science diagrams.
vocabulary.usage: Say: 'This map is drawn with meticulous care.'

vocabulary.meaning: Certain to happen; cannot be avoided.
vocabulary.explanation: Getting wet in a monsoon downpour without an umbrella is inevitable!
vocabulary.example: Change is inevitable as we grow up.
vocabulary.usage: Say: 'With so little practice, the loss was inevitable.'

vocabulary.meaning: Very bright, clear or detailed.
vocabulary.explanation: Vivid colours pop; a vivid dream feels almost real.
vocabulary.example: She described the festival in vivid detail.
vocabulary.usage: Say: 'I have a vivid memory of my first day at school.'

vocabulary.meaning: To think deeply about something.
vocabulary.explanation: When you sit quietly and think hard about a big question, you contemplate it.
vocabulary.example: He contemplated the stars from the rooftop.
vocabulary.usage: Say: 'I need time to contemplate my choice.'

vocabulary.meaning: Working hard and carefully.
vocabulary.explanation: A diligent student finishes homework carefully and on time.
vocabulary.example: The diligent farmer worked from sunrise to sunset.
vocabulary.usage: Say: 'Thank you for your diligent effort.'

vocabulary.meaning: The ability to understand and share someone's feelings.
vocabulary.explanation: Empathy is imagining how a friend feels and caring about it.
vocabulary.example: She showed empathy when her friend lost the match.

vocabulary.meaning: Careful not to waste money or resources.
vocabulary.explanation: A frugal person saves money and avoids waste.
vocabulary.example: Being frugal, Grandpa reuses every jar.

vocabulary.meaning: Using new and creative ideas.
vocabulary.explanation: An innovative invention solves a problem in a brand-new way.
vocabulary.example: ISRO used innovative technology for Chandrayaan.

vocabulary.meaning: Extremely happy and celebrating.
vocabulary.explanation: When your team wins the final over, the crowd is jubilant!
vocabulary.example: Jubilant fans danced after India won.
vocabulary.usage: Say: 'The class was jubilant about the holiday.'

vocabulary.meaning: Feeling slow and without energy.
vocabulary.explanation: When you feel too sleepy and lazy to move, you are lethargic.
vocabulary.usage: Say: 'I feel lethargic after skipping breakfast.'

vocabulary.meaning: Giving the feeling that something bad will happen.
vocabulary.explanation: Dark clouds and thunder can feel ominous.
vocabulary.example: An ominous silence filled the old house.

vocabulary.meaning: Dealing with things in a sensible, practical way.
vocabulary.explanation: A pragmatic person chooses what actually works.
vocabulary.example: Taking the metro was a pragmatic choice in traffic.

vocabulary.meaning: Not wanting to do something.
vocabulary.explanation: If you drag your feet to clean your room, you're reluctant!
vocabulary.example: He was reluctant to jump into the cold pool.
vocabulary.usage: Say: 'I was reluctant at first, but it was fun.'

vocabulary.meaning: Calm, peaceful and untroubled.
vocabulary.explanation: A still lake at sunrise feels serene.
vocabulary.example: The hill station was serene and green.
vocabulary.usage: Say: 'The garden is so serene in the morning.'

vocabulary.meaning: Holding firmly to a goal; not giving up.
vocabulary.explanation: A tenacious player keeps chasing the ball till the last second.
vocabulary.example: The tenacious climber reached the summit.

vocabulary.meaning: Clear enough to see through; also honest and open.
vocabulary.explanation: Glass is transparent. An honest person is transparent too!
vocabulary.usage: Say: 'Let's be transparent about our mistakes.'

vocabulary.meaning: Able to do many different things well.
vocabulary.explanation: A versatile player can bat, bowl and field brilliantly.

vocabulary.meaning: Careful because something could be dangerous.
vocabulary.explanation: Being wary means watching out — like when a stranger offers you sweets.
vocabulary.example: Be wary of unknown links online.

vocabulary.meaning: Full of energy and enthusiasm for something.
vocabulary.explanation: A zealous fan cheers louder than anyone else!
vocabulary.example: The zealous volunteers cleaned the whole beach.
vocabulary.usage: Say: 'She is zealous about saving animals.'

vocabulary.meaning: Able to continue without harming the environment.
vocabulary.explanation: Sustainable choices protect Earth for the future — like using cloth bags.
vocabulary.example: Solar power is a sustainable energy source.

vocabulary.meaning: To work together with others.
vocabulary.explanation: When your group builds a project together, you collaborate.
vocabulary.example: We collaborated on a model of the solar system.

vocabulary.meaning: A result of an action.
vocabulary.explanation: If you forget your umbrella, getting wet is the consequence!

vocabulary.meaning: An idea that can be tested to see if it is true.
vocabulary.explanation: Scientists make a hypothesis, then test it with an experiment!
vocabulary.example: Our hypothesis was that plants grow faster in sunlight.

vocabulary.meaning: Able to express ideas clearly.
vocabulary.explanation: An articulate person explains things so everyone understands.
vocabulary.usage: Say: 'You were very articulate in the debate.'

vocabulary.meaning: Existing in large amounts; more than enough.
vocabulary.explanation: In the mango season, mangoes are abundant!
vocabulary.usage: Say: 'Fresh fruit is abundant in summer.'

grammar.title: Nouns
grammar.explanation: A noun is a NAMING word. It names a person, animal, place or thing. Teacher, cat, Delhi and pencil are all nouns!

exercises.hint: A noun names a thing you can point at.
Where do you go every morning?

exercises.q: Which word is NOT a noun?
exercises.hint: One of these is an action.

exercises.q: Find the noun: 'My grandma makes tasty ladoos.'

grammar.title: Pronouns
grammar.explanation: A pronoun takes the place of a noun so we don't repeat it. Instead of 'Riya is kind. Riya helps me', we say 'Riya is kind. SHE helps me.' Pronouns: I, you, he, she, it, we, they.

examples.sentence: The cat is hungry. **It** wants milk.
Meera and I are friends. **We** walk to school.

exercises.q: Sara likes music. ___ sings every day.
The boys are playing. ___ are happy.
My bicycle is new. ___ is red.
Rahul and I are cousins. ___ live in Pune.

grammar.title: Verbs
grammar.explanation: A verb is an ACTION word. It tells us what someone or something does: run, eat, sing, think, write. Every sentence needs a verb!

exercises.q: Find the verb: 'Tara reads a book.'

exercises.hint: What sound does a dog make?

exercises.q: Find the verb: 'The children painted a mural.'

grammar.title: Adjectives
grammar.explanation: An adjective is a DESCRIBING word. It tells us more about a noun — its colour, size, shape, feeling or number. 'A BIG, RED balloon.'

exercises.q: Find the adjective: 'She wore a yellow dress.'
Find the adjective: 'The curious monkey opened the box.'

grammar.title: Articles: a, an, the
grammar.explanation: Use 'a' before consonant sounds (a cat), 'an' before vowel sounds (an apple, an hour), and 'the' for something specific (the sun, the book I lent you).

examples.note: an + vowel sound, a + consonant sound

grammar.title: Prepositions
grammar.explanation: Prepositions tell us WHERE or WHEN something is: in, on, under, behind, between, at, before, after. 'The cat is UNDER the table.'

exercises.hint: The fish is inside the water.
Riya on one side, Aman on the other.
Use this for an exact time.

grammar.title: Punctuation
grammar.explanation: Punctuation marks help readers. Start sentences with a capital letter. End with a full stop (.), a question mark (?) or an exclamation mark (!). Use commas (,) in lists.

examples.sentence: I bought apples**,** mangoes and bananas.

exercises.q: Pick the right ending: 'What a lovely garden'

options: I like red, blue and green.
I like, red blue and green.
I, like red blue, and green.

exercises.hint: Days of the week are special names.
'I' is always capital, and end with a full stop.

grammar.title: Building Sentences
grammar.explanation: A sentence needs a SUBJECT (who) and a VERB (does what), and it must make sense. 'The cat (subject) sleeps (verb).' Order matters in English: Subject → Verb → Object.

exercises.q: What is the subject? 'The teacher smiled.'
Which is NOT a complete sentence?

options: We went to the zoo yesterday.
exercises.hint: Read each aloud — which sounds right?

grammar.title: Adverbs
grammar.explanation: An adverb describes a VERB — HOW, WHEN or WHERE something happens. Many adverbs end in -ly: quickly, softly, happily. Others: soon, here, always.

exercises.hint: It describes HOW an action happens.

grammar.title: Conjunctions
grammar.explanation: Conjunctions are JOINING words: and, but, or, so, because. They connect words or ideas. 'I was hungry, SO I ate a sandwich.'

exercises.q: I wanted to play, ___ it was raining.
He was tired, ___ he went to bed early.
We stayed inside ___ it was too hot.

grammar.title: Tenses
grammar.explanation: Tense shows WHEN an action happens. Past: I played. Present: I play / I am playing. Future: I will play.

examples.sentence: Tomorrow we **will go** to the beach.

exercises.q: Which sentence is in the past tense?

grammar.title: Subject–Verb Agreement
grammar.explanation: The verb must match the subject. One person/thing (he, she, it, the dog) → add -s: 'She runs.' More than one (they, we, the dogs) → no -s: 'They run.'

exercises.q: The box of crayons ___ on the desk.

grammar.title: Active & Passive Voice
grammar.explanation: Active voice: the subject DOES the action — 'Ravi wrote the letter.' Passive voice: the subject RECEIVES the action — 'The letter was written by Ravi.' Active is usually clearer; passive is useful when the doer is unknown.

examples.sentence: Passive: The meal **was cooked** by the chef.

options: The mouse was chased by the cat.

exercises.q: Make it passive: 'Asha painted the picture.'
options: The picture was painted by Asha.
Asha was painted by the picture.
exercises.hint: Object becomes subject + was + past participle.

exercises.q: Make it active: 'The match was won by our team.'

options: The song was sung by the choir.

grammar.title: Direct & Indirect Speech
grammar.explanation: Direct speech quotes exact words: She said, "I am tired." Indirect (reported) speech reports them without quotes, usually shifting tense and pronouns: She said that she was tired.

examples.sentence: Indirect: Raj said that he liked mangoes.
Direct: "Are you coming?" asked Mom. → Mom asked if I was coming.

exercises.q: Indirect of: She said, "I am happy."
options: She said that she was happy.
She said that I am happy.

exercises.q: Indirect of: He said, "I will come."
options: He said that he would come.
He said that I will come.
Tom told that he is late.

exercises.q: Indirect of: "Do you like chess?" she asked me.
options: She asked me if I liked chess.
She asked me do you like chess.

exercises.q: Indirect of: The teacher said, "Open your books."
options: The teacher told us to open our books.

Pip was sad. 'I am too small. Nobody can see me,' said Pip.
But down below, a girl named Anu looked up. 'I see you, little star!' she said.
Pip was so happy that Pip began to shine bright, bright, bright!

pages.text: The monsoon rain fell all night. In the morning, Kabir saw an enormous puddle outside his gate.
A tiny frog sat in the middle of the puddle. 'Ribbit! This is my lake,' it seemed to say.
Kabir and his sister Zoya made paper boats. They were careful not to splash the frog.
The boats sailed across the puddle. Then a rainbow appeared in the sky. It was the best morning ever!

pages.text: In the corner of an ancient museum in Jaipur stood a clockwork elephant, covered in dust. Nobody had wound its golden key for a hundred years.
One rainy afternoon, curious Ishita noticed the key glimmer. She looked around, then turned it — once, twice, three times.
With a whir and a click, the elephant opened its eyes. 'Thank you,' it trumpeted softly. 'I have been waiting for someone with courage.'
The elephant showed Ishita a mysterious map hidden in its saddle. It led to a garden where the city's lost songs were kept.
Together they returned the songs to the city. That evening, every street in Jaipur was filled with music — and Ishita was delighted.

pages.text: Aarav's school had built a small satellite receiver for the science fair. On the night before the fair, it picked up a faint, repeating signal — not from space, but from the coral reef off the coast.
His teacher, Ms. Fernandes, was sceptical. 'Form a hypothesis,' she said, 'then test it meticulously.' Aarav's hypothesis: the signal came from an old ocean sensor.
With the local marine-research team, the class sailed out at dawn. The water was serene, but the coral looked pale — bleached by warming seas, an ominous sign.
They found the sensor tangled in a fishing net. It had been broadcasting temperature warnings for weeks, but no one had been listening.
Aarav's project didn't win first prize, but the city installed new reef sensors because of it. Sometimes, the most innovative idea is simply paying attention.

pages.text: In a small village lived Meena, a potter. She made pots that were strong and beautiful.
One day a rich trader paid her too much money by mistake. Meena saw the extra coins.
She ran after the trader. 'Sir, you gave me too much!' she said, and returned the coins.
The trader smiled. 'You are honest. From today, I will buy all my pots from you.' Meena's work grew and grew.

pages.text: On the far side of the moon there is a library. Its books float, because there is very little gravity!
Astronaut Leela and her robot friend Bolt visit every Sunday. Bolt reads the books aloud in a funny, beeping voice.
One book was empty. 'This book is waiting for a new story,' said the librarian, a gentle old owl in a space suit.
Leela wrote about Earth — its oceans, mango trees and festivals. Now every moon visitor can read it!
